title: Boosting Explainability through Selective Rationalization in Pre-trained Language Models

problem.claim: Applying selective rationalization to pre-trained language models can produce degenerate, failed, sub-optimal, or meaningless rationales.

gap.claim: Existing rationalization frameworks do not adequately address the failure problems that arise when applied to pre-trained language models.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes Pre-trained Language Model's Rationalization (PLMR), which splits a pre-trained language model into a generator and a predictor while providing interpretable rationales.
PLMR's generator prunes irrelevant tokens to alleviate token homogeneity, while its predictor uses full-text information to standardize predictions.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on two widely used datasets across multiple pre-trained language models demonstrate the reported effectiveness of PLMR in addressing the stated challenge.
Code is reported as available in the linked GitHub repository.

narrative_sequence.summary: The widespread use of pre-trained language models has increased concerns about their explainability.
Selective rationalization selects human-intelligible input subsets as rationales for predictions.
Existing rationalization frameworks can fail on pre-trained language models, producing sub-optimal or meaningless rationales and damaging trust in the methods.
The paper attributes the problems primarily to token homogeneity and proposes PLMR, which separates generation and prediction and uses token pruning with full-text prediction.
Experiments across two datasets and multiple pre-trained language models are reported as demonstrating PLMR's effectiveness.

source_observation.claim: The paper identifies token homogeneity in pre-trained-language-model outputs as the primary contributor to rationalization failures.

interpretation.claim: Rationale quality may improve when the rationale generator is encouraged to remove irrelevant or redundant tokens.

application.claim: For explainability systems built around pre-trained language models, consider separating rationale generation from prediction and pruning irrelevant tokens during rationale generation.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach generalizes beyond the reported datasets, models, or tasks.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, tasks, pre-trained language models, baselines, metrics, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not describe the mechanism used to identify or prune irrelevant tokens.
The abstract does not provide details about the generator-predictor architecture or training procedure.
The abstract does not independently verify the reported effectiveness or code availability.
